title: Arjuna's Despair
summary: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna asks his charioteer Krishna to drive out between the two armies. Seeing friends, teachers and kin arrayed on both sides, Arjuna loses heart and lets his bow fall, unwilling to fight a war that will kill his own family.

title: Knowledge and Reason
summary: Krishna answers Arjuna's grief with the book's core teaching: the self is eternal and is never really born or killed, only the body changes. He introduces steady wisdom, acting without clinging to results, and the discipline of a mind that is not tossed about by pleasure and pain.

title: The Path of Action
summary: Krishna explains that no one can simply stop acting, so the real choice is how to act. He teaches selfless action performed as duty and as an offering, without attachment to personal gain, as the way to stay free while still fully engaged in the world.

title: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
summary: Krishna describes himself as appearing across ages to restore right action, and explains how action can be performed as a form of knowledge and sacrifice, burning away its usual binding effect when done with understanding instead of craving.

title: Renunciation and Action Reconciled
summary: Krishna shows that renouncing action and performing action skillfully lead to the same end when done without selfish attachment. True renunciation is an inner state of non-clinging, not simply withdrawing from the world.

title: The Practice of Meditation
summary: Krishna gives practical instruction on meditation: posture, a steady seat, moderation in food and rest, and a mind trained to rest evenly on the self. He reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on this path is never wasted, even if the practice is imperfect.

title: Knowledge and Wisdom
summary: Krishna describes his own nature as both the visible world and the unseen power behind it, explains why people turn toward or away from this truth, and distinguishes those who seek him for passing wants from those who seek him for himself.

title: The Imperishable Absolute
summary: Arjuna asks what happens at the moment of death. Krishna explains how a person's final thought shapes their next state, and contrasts the paths that lead back into the cycle of rebirth with the path that leads beyond it.

title: The Royal Knowledge, the Royal Secret
summary: Krishna shares what he calls the most confidential teaching: that he sustains the universe while remaining untouched by it, and that sincere devotion, however simple, is received completely regardless of a person's background.

title: Divine Glories
summary: Krishna lists examples of his presence in the world, naming himself as the best or most essential example within many categories, from forces of nature to human excellences, as a way of showing that everything outstanding points back to one source.

title: The Vision of the Universal Form
summary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his vast cosmic form containing all beings and all time. Overwhelmed and afraid, Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his familiar human form, having seen what lies behind it.

title: The Path of Devotion
summary: Krishna compares devotion to a personal form of the divine with meditation on the formless absolute, and says the devotional path is easier for most people. He then describes the qualities of a devotee he holds especially dear.

title: The Field and Its Knower
summary: Krishna distinguishes the 'field' — the body and the material world of changing qualities — from the 'knower of the field' — the conscious self that witnesses it. Recognizing this distinction clearly is described as true knowledge.

title: The Three Qualities of Nature
summary: Krishna explains the three fundamental qualities — clarity, restless passion, and inertia — that mix in different proportions in every mind and situation, and describes how someone rises above all three to reach lasting peace.

title: The Supreme Person
summary: Using the image of an inverted tree with roots above and branches below, Krishna describes the world as a reflection, and points to the imperishable, unconditioned reality that supports it as the highest truth to recognize.

title: The Divine and the Demonic Natures
summary: Krishna contrasts two sets of inner tendencies: qualities such as fearlessness, honesty and self-control that lead toward freedom, and qualities such as hypocrisy, greed and anger that lead toward bondage and suffering.

title: The Three Kinds of Faith
summary: Krishna explains that people's faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and giving all take on the character of whichever of the three qualities dominates them, and that the spirit behind an action matters as much as the action itself.

title: Freedom Through Surrender
summary: In the closing discourse, Krishna draws the whole teaching together: act according to one's own nature and duty, offer the results to the highest good, and find freedom not by refusing action but by releasing attachment to it. Arjuna says his doubts have left him and he is ready to act.
